name: Relative Peeling Failures Transfer to Forbidden PC-Minors
statement: Let rooted ample $R$ peel but not to its root, and suppose every elementary root-preserving restriction or contraction of $R$ peels to its induced root. Let nonempty ample peelable $K\subseteq A\subseteq Q_E$ have all coordinates active, and assume the same for $R$. Then $P_R(A,K)$ is a forbidden pc-minor for corner-peelable ample families exactly when $A$ does not peel down to $K$, while $\mu A$ peels down to $\mu K$ for every elementary restriction or contraction $\mu$ on an old coordinate for which $\mu K$ is nonempty.
proof: An old-coordinate operation commutes with the attachment: $\mu P_R(A,K)=P_R(\mu A,\mu K)$. On a new coordinate, root-preserving restriction and contraction replace $R$ by the corresponding rooted image, while the opposite restriction is a product over $K$; all three peel by hypothesis. If an old-coordinate image of $K$ is empty, the image is merely $\mu A$. Otherwise the attachment theorem says it peels exactly when $\mu A$ peels down to $\mu K$. The same theorem detects nonpeelability of the original attachment, giving both directions.
